pr_body:
Fixes #20291

pr_comments: This looks good to me (mild preference for `!= 1` rather than `== 0`, but PR author has ultimate choice in these things) - I would love to see this approved and merged
Removing `approval: otc review pending` as @paulidale has approved
I presume tests aren't needed for this fix?

> I presume tests aren't needed for this fix?

The test policy is here:
https://www.openssl.org/policies/technical/testing.html

In this case I'd say this exemption applies:

> A test may be omitted where writing the test would result in disproportionately more effort than writing the code being tested.

In general we of course prefer tests for all PRs, but there are no existing tests for the "speed" app at all - so writing a test for this small fix would be very difficult.

24 hours has passed since 'approval: done' was set, but as this PR has been updated in that time the label 'approval: ready to merge' is not being automatically set.  Please review the updates and set the label manually.

Merged.

Should this have gone to 3.1 and 3.0 too?
I think this code was in master only (and definitely not in 3.0).
I've confirmed that the change in #15905, which introduced the problem, is not in `3.1`

issue_context.title: "Error finalizing cipher loop" when running openssl speed -evp
issue_context.body:
Since commit 98283a61f5 I am seeing

```
$ perl Configure darwin64-arm64 no-shared no-threads no-async -Wimplicit-function-declaration && time make -j10 && echo && DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=. apps/openssl speed -evp aes-128-gcm
:
		apps/libapps.a -lssl -lcrypto  

real	0m34.00s
user	2m56.95s
sys	0m43.71s

Doing AES-128-GCM for 3s on 16 size blocks: Error finalizing cipher loop
197335957 AES-128-GCM's in 3.00s
Doing AES-128-GCM for 3s on 64 size blocks: Error finalizing cipher loop
135033964 AES-128-GCM's in 3.00s
Doing AES-128-GCM for 3s on 256 size blocks: Error finalizing cipher loop
53776484 AES-128-GCM's in 3.00s
Doing AES-128-GCM for 3s on 1024 size blocks: Error finalizing cipher loop
21636816 AES-128-GCM's in 3.00s
Doing AES-128-GCM for 3s on 8192 size blocks: Error finalizing cipher loop
3051110 AES-128-GCM's in 2.99s
Doing AES-128-GCM for 3s on 16384 size blocks: Error finalizing cipher loop
1537926 AES-128-GCM's in 3.00s
version: 3.2.0-dev
built on: Wed Feb 15 00:10:38 2023 UTC
options: bn(64,64)
compiler: cc -fPIC -arch arm64 -O3 -Wall -Wimplicit-function-declaration -DL_ENDIAN -DOPENSSL_PIC -DOPENSSL_BUILDING_OPENSSL -DNDEBUG
CPUINFO: OPENSSL_armcap=0x187d
The 'numbers' are in 1000s of bytes per second processed.
type             16 bytes     64 bytes    256 bytes   1024 bytes   8192 bytes  16384 bytes
AES-128-GCM    1052458.44k  2880724.57k  4588926.63k  7385366.53k  8359429.14k  8399126.53k
```

If I revert `98283a61f5` and build, I get

```
$ perl Configure darwin64-arm64 no-shared no-threads no-async -Wimplicit-function-declaration && time make -j10 && echo && DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=. apps/openssl speed -evp aes-128-gcm
:
		apps/libapps.a -lssl -lcrypto  

real	0m33.77s
user	2m55.24s
sys	0m43.58s

Doing AES-128-GCM for 3s on 16 size blocks: 198213155 AES-128-GCM's in 3.00s
Doing AES-128-GCM for 3s on 64 size blocks: 136294089 AES-128-GCM's in 3.00s
Doing AES-128-GCM for 3s on 256 size blocks: 53526662 AES-128-GCM's in 3.00s
Doing AES-128-GCM for 3s on 1024 size blocks: 20822216 AES-128-GCM's in 2.96s
Doing AES-128-GCM for 3s on 8192 size blocks: 2997378 AES-128-GCM's in 2.97s
Doing AES-128-GCM for 3s on 16384 size blocks: 1535425 AES-128-GCM's in 3.00s
version: 3.2.0-dev
built on: Wed Feb 15 00:15:13 2023 UTC
options: bn(64,64)
compiler: cc -fPIC -arch arm64 -O3 -Wall -Wimplicit-function-declaration -DL_ENDIAN -DOPENSSL_PIC -DOPENSSL_BUILDING_OPENSSL -DNDEBUG
CPUINFO: OPENSSL_armcap=0x187d
The 'numbers' are in 1000s of bytes per second processed.
type             16 bytes     64 bytes    256 bytes   1024 bytes   8192 bytes  16384 bytes
AES-128-GCM    1057136.83k  2907607.23k  4567608.49k  7203361.21k  8267515.35k  8385467.73k
```

Part of the changes in that commit are

```
     if (decrypt)
-        EVP_DecryptFinal_ex(ctx, buf, &outl);
+        rc = EVP_DecryptFinal_ex(ctx, buf, &outl);
     else
-        EVP_EncryptFinal_ex(ctx, buf, &outl);
+        rc = EVP_EncryptFinal_ex(ctx, buf, &outl);
+
+    if (rc <= 1)
+        BIO_printf(bio_err, "Error finalizing cipher loop\n");
     return count;
 }
```

but `man EVP_DecryptFinal_ex` says

```
EVP_DecryptFinal_ex() returns 0 if the decrypt failed or 1 for success.
```

So: is the test for `rc <= 1` correct?

(I'm raising this as an issue because I think I've seen a number of changes recently regarding return values, and I haven't checked them all: this one was literally in my face!)
comments: Looks like a bug to me. Probably should be `<= 0`

review_comments: Would it be better to use `!= 1`? Yes, they should be equivalent if the function only returns 0 or 1, but go for "not success" rather than "is failure"
